question: Who invented the mop fly?
answer: Jim Estes of Bryson City, North Carolina invented the mop fly in the late 1990s after discovering microfiber mop material at a local Dollar Store. He tied the spongy nubs onto a hook with a bead head and dubbing collar — originally to imitate the large sourwood worms that fall from trees in Western NC during summer. Mac Brown and Jim Estes have been friends since the mid-1980s and Bryson City remains the birthplace of one of the most controversial and effective fly patterns in the sport.

question: What does the mop fly imitate?
answer: Originally tied to imitate sourwood worms — large terrestrial caterpillars that fall from trees in June through August in Western North Carolina. In other colors the mop fly imitates crane fly larvae, aquatic worms, and various soft-bodied invertebrates. In chartreuse it is one of the most effective patterns on the Tuckasegee and Nantahala rivers year-round regardless of what it technically imitates — the material has action, color, and bulk that trout find irresistible.

question: Why was the mop fly banned from fly fishing competitions?
answer: The mop fly was banned from several fly fishing competitions because it was simply too effective — producing fish at a rate that gave competitors using it an unfair advantage. It had already won multiple USA Fly Fishing Team Youth gold medals in European competition before the controversy peaked. Jim Estes submitted it to Umpqua Feather Merchants who declined it as a regional pattern — then added it to their 2018 catalog as the Umpqua Mop after it went global.

question: What colors work best for mop flies?
answer: Chartreuse was the original color — matching the sourwood worm that inspired the pattern. Tan mop flies are Jim Estes's preferred pattern for the Nantahala River as a crane fly larvae imitation and produce year-round. Olive, pink, and white are also productive depending on water clarity and conditions. The material itself — not the color — is what gives the mop fly its action and effectiveness.

question: Where can I fish mop flies near Bryson City NC?
answer: The Tuckasegee River delayed harvest section and the Nantahala River are the two most productive mop fly waters near Bryson City — the rivers where Jim Estes originally developed and proved the pattern. Mac Brown Fly Fish guides both rivers year-round with mop fly rigs as part of the standard nymph rotation. All gear including flies is provided on every guided trip.
